title: PwC Annual Threat Dynamics 2026: Cyber threats in motion

cards.title: Identity is the ultimate battleground
cards.description: PwC's headline narrative for 2026 reframes the perimeter: adversaries are no longer breaking in, they are logging in by abusing credentials, session tokens, and federated access to bypass traditional defences.
cards.quote: "Adversaries are increasingly choosing to log in rather than break in, exploiting credentials, session tokens, and federated access to bypass traditional perimeter defences. Identity has become the ultimate battleground."

cards.title: 63% of manufacturing attacks are cybercrime-motivated
cards.description: Manufacturing remained a top sector target in PwC's 2026 dataset, with the majority of observed incidents driven by financially motivated cybercrime rather than espionage or sabotage. Incidents frequently cascaded into broader supply-chain disruption.

cards.title: Manufacturing attack motivations, 2025
cards.description: PwC's breakdown of motivations behind attacks on the manufacturing sector shows cybercrime dominating, followed by state-aligned espionage. Sabotage and hacktivism account for small but strategically meaningful slices of activity against operational technology environments.

cards.title: Threat actors treat AI as core tradecraft
cards.description: PwC's incident-response team reports that AI-driven threats are now the most frequently raised client concern, with adversaries integrating generative AI into reconnaissance, malware development, and multilingual social engineering pipelines.
cards.quote: "Threat actors are embracing AI not as an enhancement but as a core component of their tradecraft, using it to automate reconnaissance, craft highly convincing phishing campaigns, accelerate malware development, and scale social engineering across languages and platforms."

cards.title: AI-automated spear-phishing click-through 4.5x generic phishing
cards.description: PwC cites research showing AI-automated spear-phishing emails achieved a 54% click-through rate versus 12% for generic phishing, underscoring how generative AI raises the conversion rate of social-engineering campaigns at scale.

cards.title: 88% of web-app breaches involve stolen credentials
cards.description: PwC reinforces its identity-first thesis with Verizon data showing the overwhelming majority of breaches in web-application attacks rely on stolen credentials — a key reason identity remains the primary attack vector heading into 2026.

cards.title: Identity abuse is the top entry point at 30%
cards.description: PwC cites IBM data showing abuse of user identities is the single most common initial entry point for intrusions, reinforcing the report's central finding that identity has overtaken exploits and email as the primary attack vector.

cards.title: AI-related incidents up 56.4% YoY
cards.description: PwC cites Stanford HAI data tracking 233 AI-related incidents in 2024, a 56.4% increase over 2023 — quantitative confirmation that adversarial AI exposure is growing alongside enterprise AI adoption.

cards.title: AI governance gaps are nearly universal
cards.description: PwC highlights two governance failures that explain why AI is amplifying risk: nearly all organisations experiencing AI security incidents lacked proper access controls, and most have no AI governance policy in place at all.

cards.title: GenAI prompts to SaaS apps up 6x to 18,000/month
cards.description: PwC cites Netskope data showing organisational prompts to SaaS GenAI applications grew sixfold from roughly 3,000 to 18,000 per month, with an average of 223 GenAI data-policy violations per organisation per month — a rapidly expanding shadow-AI surface.

cards.title: Personal AI app use for work falls to 47%
cards.description: Personal AI app use for work declined from 78% to 47%, reflecting the maturing of enterprise-sanctioned AI tooling — though the gap is now being filled by sanctioned SaaS GenAI usage, which has grown sixfold.

cards.title: Supply-chain compromises up nearly 4x since 2020
cards.description: PwC cites IBM X-Force telemetry showing supply-chain and third-party compromise incidents have grown nearly fourfold since 2020, validating the report's emphasis on managing risk beyond the direct enterprise perimeter.

cards.title: Top OT/IIoT security challenges for executives
cards.description: PwC's executive-concerns data highlights two structural OT/IIoT security barriers: a shortage of qualified personnel and unclear governance over who owns OT security — both blocking the convergence of IT and OT defence programmes.

series.name: Share citing as top OT/IIoT challenge

cards.title: Blurring boundaries between motivations
cards.description: PwC argues the traditional clean lines between cybercrime, espionage, and influence operations have dissolved — with ransomware operators monetising strategic data, state actors using criminal tooling, and DPRK-linked operations industrialising fraudulent employment.
cards.quote: "The boundaries between motivations continued to blur, as ransomware operators sold strategically sensitive data, espionage-motivated threat actors leveraged cyber criminal tooling, and North Korea-based threat actors industrialised fraudulent employment and cryptocurrency theft at unprecedented scale."

cards.title: DPRK industrialised fraudulent IT-worker scheme
cards.description: North Korea-linked operations scaled fraudulent remote-employment schemes and cryptocurrency theft to unprecedented levels in 2025, with stolen identities used to place operatives inside global enterprises while funnelling salaries and stolen funds to the regime.

cards.title: China-based actor deployed autonomous AI red-team agent
cards.description: Following the release of ReaperAI, a penetration-testing AI agent, PwC documented a China-based threat actor deploying a comparable tool capable of autonomous reconnaissance and exploit execution — an early example of agentic AI in offensive operations.
cards.quote: "Following the release of ReaperAI, a China-based threat actor deployed a comparable tool capable of autonomous reconnaissance and exploit execution."

cards.title: AWM sector hit by BEC, ransomware, and crypto heists
cards.description: PwC's sector view of asset & wealth management (AWM) and financial services shows convergence of business-email compromise with AI-generated deepfakes, ransomware operations, and large heists targeting cryptocurrency platforms — all leveraging identity abuse as the common pivot.

cards.title: Healthcare ransomware crosses into life-safety risk
cards.description: PwC continues to flag healthcare and hospitality as ransomware-exposed sectors where attacks disrupt operations and, in healthcare specifically, can become life-threatening — elevating ransomware from an IT-availability issue to a patient-safety issue.

cards.title: Adversaries deploy full-stack tradecraft
cards.description: PwC characterises the 2026 threat landscape as one where adversaries move fluidly across identity, cloud, edge, and application layers — a 'full-stack' approach that breaks single-layer defensive models and demands integrated, identity-anchored security architecture.
cards.quote: "We are seeing an increasingly capable and adaptive threat landscape in which adversaries employ full-stack tradecraft and are fluidly navigating identity, cloud, edge, and application layers with unprecedented precision."

cards.title: AI is the #1 cyber investment priority
cards.description: PwC reports that AI-driven defence has become the top cybersecurity investment priority among security leaders heading into 2026, paralleling the rise of AI-driven offence. AI is now identified as the most frequently raised client concern by PwC's incident-response team.

cards.title: Post-quantum readiness becomes urgent
cards.description: PwC flags quantum computing as a near-term cryptographic risk and pairs it with rapidly expanding SaaS ecosystems as the two emerging surfaces defenders must instrument now — recommending post-quantum cryptography transition planning and SaaS-identity governance.
cards.quote: "Quantum computing threats to cryptography and expanding SaaS ecosystems widening attack surfaces make post-quantum cryptography transition an urgent strategic priority."
